# Public-effect boundary: preserved first study

The [original context](first/README.first.md), [source inventory](first/first-sources.json),
[observations](first/observations-first.json), [analysis](first/analysis-first.json)
and [complete frozen inventory](first/freeze.json) retain the informed study
before #355 implementation. All 163 listed files and the freeze itself are
copied byte-for-byte; absolute temporary paths remain historical data.

Nineteen original projects contain 43 source/manifest files. The 38 actual
finite/selected checks retain eight policy-gap acceptances and eighteen
false-pure refusals. Changing only an Observe library body from identity to
reset changed the external Unitary result, exposing implementation inference
across the public boundary. The selected reset/Observe positive instead met an
unsupported-profile refusal; its mistaken prediction is preserved.

This integration note was written after those observations. Their original
record does not identify an exact model build or a checked Git source revision;
none is reconstructed as contemporaneous provenance. The informed authoring
context and observed CLI/kernel digests are retained with their stated limits.
The study is neither a blind benchmark nor native process attestation.

`scripts/test_public_effects_first.py` checks inert historical identities and
record consistency. It never executes recorded commands. Current source/API,
provider, transformation and actual-operation regressions are separate tests.
`scripts/test_public_effects.py` constructs 38 new current CLI checks with
independently specified expectations over the unchanged 19 projects. It reads
only their frozen source inventory, never historical commands or predictions;
current checks retain the concrete reset-profile refusal and check actual scope
disclosures. Its results are separate from the preserved first observations.
No historical source, prediction or diagnostic is repaired, and the study
supplies no general source/runtime proof, guarantee admission or release claim.

The [separate quantum-use contrast](quantum-use-contrast/freeze.json) retains
two more first programs and their actual diagnostics from the initially
implemented CLI, before rebuilding its repair. The unchanged caller's bare
public `fn` accepted a classical implementation behind `pub unitary`, but
refused after only the callee body acquired closed `Q<Unit>` work. That leaked
an internal quantum-use flag despite the same public declaration. Both complete
sources, raw streams, before-check context and observed executable identities
are retained. The source tree may already have contained later edits; this
record claims only the identified executable's observed behavior. These two
checks are separate from the original 38 and from the subsequent regression.
